item.title: Europe and America lose millions of Christians, Africa now largest region with 697 million believers
item.description: Christianity remains the world’s largest religion at 2.3 billion people, but its global share is shrinking as religious switching accelerates, especially in Western countries. While Europe and North America see steady decline, sub-Saharan Africa now anchors the faith’s growth. The data reveals not collapse, but a geographic and cultural shift reshaping Christianity’s global center of gravity.

item.title: JD Vance defends Trump’s racist Obama video, says it’s ‘not a real controversy’
item.description: In a recent public address, US Vice President JD Vance dismissed the uproar over a controversial AI-generated video depicting the Obamas as apes, which was circulated by former President Donald Trump. Vance emphasized that this matter has moved past the point of effective discussion and highlighted the importance of focusing on pressing issues facing the nation.

item.title: Watch: Passengers scream as Arik Air Boeing flight's left engine destroyed mid-air; plane makes emergency landing
item.description: An Arik Air Boeing 737 experienced a terrifying mid-air incident when its left engine exploded en route to Port Harcourt. Passengers witnessed the shredded engine as the plane made a safe emergency landing in Benin on a single engine. While no injuries were reported, the aircraft sustained significant damage, prompting an investigation into the cause.

item.title: Presidents Day 2026: What will be closed — banks, government offices and more
item.description: Presidents Day, observed on the third Monday of February, honored all U.S. presidents, originally established to celebrate George Washington's birthday. In 2026, it fell on February 16, leading to closures of government offices, banks, and postal services. The holiday's official name remains Washington's Birthday, though it evolved to recognize all commanders-in-chief.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Hallyu' from Seoul: How South Korea's K-wave swept India - and its darker side
item.description: South Korea's 'Korean Wave' has transformed from a niche phenomenon to a mainstream cultural force in India and across the globe, driven by K-pop, K-dramas, and lifestyle trends. This soft power surge, fueled by digital access and strategic state policy, offers a model for global influence, impacting consumption and aspirations across the nation.
item.dc:creator: Aadrita Halder and Yash Sonkar

item.title: Iran-US indirect talks: Tehran’s top diplomat travels to Geneva for second round
item.description: Iran's foreign minister heads to Geneva for crucial indirect nuclear talks with the US, mediated by Oman. This follows earlier discussions that stalled due to regional conflict. Tehran seeks economic benefits, including sanctions relief, while Washington demands a halt to uranium enrichment. Tensions remain high with potential military action looming.

item.title: Fact check: Was Erika Kirk arrested after Candace Owens raised grooming allegation about 15 year old online?
item.description: Viral social media posts and a YouTube video claimed Erika Kirk was arrested while fleeing to Israel over grooming allegations amplified by Candace Owens. Public court records and US law enforcement databases show no arrest, no investigation, and no charges against her. The screenshots behind the claim remain unverified, and no official source confirms wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Are aliens real? Here's what US ex-President Barack Obama said in podcast
item.description: Former President Barack Obama stated that aliens are real but he has not encountered them, dismissing claims of their presence at Area 51. He also revealed that upon entering office, he inquired about extraterrestrial life and was informed no such studies were underway. Obama acknowledged that unexplained aerial phenomena are taken seriously by officials.

item.title: 'Am not a politician anymore and can't be': Barack Obama reveals reason why 'Michelle would divorce' him
item.description: Barack Obama humorously stated that a return to elected office would likely end his marriage, crediting Michelle Obama's influence. He emphasized their post-presidency focus on empowering the next generation through the Obama Foundation, rather than seeking personal power. Their new Chicago center will embody this vision, fostering emerging leaders.

item.title: Marco Rubio says, US ‘not disputing’ European report blaming Russia for Navalny poisoning
item.description: US secretary of state Marco Rubio stated Washington is not disputing a report by five European nations concluding Alexei Navalny was fatally poisoned. The report identified a rare toxin from a dart frog, with Russia identified as the prime suspect. Navalny's widow declared his murder a "science-proven fact" after his death in a Russian penal colony.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: From Wall Street to Hollywood: Casey Wasserman latest hit in Epstein files fallout — read full list
item.description: Casey Wasserman, a prominent Hollywood talent agent, is selling his business following the release of Epstein files that exposed communications with Ghislaine Maxwell. Wasserman apologized for past personal mistakes impacting clients and partners. Several other individuals, including Kathy Ruemmler and Brad Karp, have also faced consequences due to their connections with Epstein revealed in the documents.

item.title: ‘A lecture from a country ranked 58th?’: Kaja Kallas fires back at Marco Rubio on free speech
item.description: Estonian official Kaja Kallas sharply responded to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's remarks on free speech. Kallas highlighted Estonia's high ranking in a freedom of speech index, contrasting it with the US's lower position, suggesting a lecture from the US was 'interesting'.
